text: Of what Isaac knows Genesis 22 says nothing. He carries the wood; he asks after the lamb; the answer which he receives leaves the question where it was. No thought or feeling is opened in him. The narrator records only that they went, both of them, together. The phrase returns, and its return takes the place of explanation. The question of Isaac's consent is allowed to appear, and is then set aside unresolved. In this account the logic of Obedience settles all, and leaves nothing unaccounted for.
